summary: Page 1: typed list of the 31 owners of Paihia 1D1E2 (area 19:2:27 = 7.9596 ha; 216.666 shares; file no. 9294), with later strike-throughs pointing to successor list numbers. Pages 2–6: handwritten schedule of ownership orders, entries 32–80 (1979–1995). Whānau entries: no. 25 "Rirena Rihari Matiu or Rirena Arana [Arama]" 5.317 → 20 Oct 1981 (AT 12/360) to Lucy Nicholas, Makura Arama, Hannah Wano and Charlie Arama equally — Rirena's successors, a year after her death; Makura (Makura Albert Cassidy Arama) → 1993 to Christine Anne Arama, Hannah Margaret Adams, Jason Arama. No. 6 "Hira Rihari Matui" 5.318 (still on title) and no. 23 "Rata Rihari Matui" 5.317 (→ 1994 to six successors) — two further Rihari Matiu children alongside Rirena, each with the same share. No. 2 "Arapeta Piriparaihe" = Arapeta Peri Paraihe or Albert Peri → 1982 via the Public Trustee to nine children (Henry, Richard, Frances, Wiremu, Annette, Alfred, Anthony, John Peri (Paraihe) and Jane Takurua). Nos 7 and 17, Hone and Te Okena Piriparaihe, 5.318 each, still standing unsucceeded. The six equal 5.317/5.318 shares (Arapeta, Hone, Te Okena; Hira, Rata, Rirena) total 31.905 — consistent with one earlier interest divided in two (Ruhia Matiu Wiripo's three sons; Rihari Matiu's three children), i.e. an interest that came down from Matiu Wiripo through both a daughter (Ruhia) and a son (Rihari). The Atama/Manihera owners are the Atama Matiu line (Wati Manihera absorbing five interests 1981–82).

title: Paihia 1D1E — schedule of ownership orders: successions to Pati Wharewaka (1940) and Atama Matiu (1952)
summary: One handwritten page of the "Schedule of Ownership Orders" for Paihia 1D1E (shares 216.666). Two successions: Pati Wharewaka (list no. 2, 20.000; S.O. 13.8.40) to Mane, Takuira, Topia, Paterihi, Manuera and Iwa Atama (1/7 each) and to Pita, Takuira, Ihipeti, Nikora, Wati and Katarina Manihera (1/42 each); and Atama Matiu (list no. 1, 85.000; S.O. 28.3.52) to Toma Atama (3/17) and the same six Atama children (2/17 each) and six Manihera grandchildren (1/51 each). The Paihia 1D title came through Matiu Wiripo (succession from Pirini Wiripo, 1910 — doc 1445102), so "Atama Matiu" is very probably a son of Matiu Wiripo, i.e. a brother of Rihari Matiu, and Pati Wharewaka his wife — a Matiu–Wharewaka marriage in the same generation as Ria Hone Wharewaka (Peri Paraihe's daughter, whose "Hone Wharewaka" is presumably a married name). "Topia" (Topia Atama) is the name that later appears as Wati Ratahi Topia and Erina Rutuki Topia, successors to Ria Hone Wharewaka in Whakakoro F4.

title: Paihia 1D1C — succession order schedule 1929–1950 (7 pages): Ruhia Peri Matiu and the Peri Matiu children
summary: Seven pages of Form 16 succession order schedules for Paihia 1D1C. Key whānau entries (p.1, all 3 July 1929, HK 10/94): three children who died young — "Roi Matiu" (1906), "Hoana Peri Matiu" (1907) and "Hana Peri Matiu" (1909) — succeeded by "Ruhia Peri Matiu, f.a." solely (Hana's half shared with Iri Tamaho Maika). This is Ruhia Matiu Wiripo, Peri Paraihe's second wife, recorded under her married form "Ruhia Peri Matiu", with a small annotation of a further name (Horomona / Paura Taitimu). In 1940 she took 1/8 of Parani Ritete alias Parani Rewi (d. 1916) alongside Iri Tamaho Maika (1/8) — an unexplained close tie to the Ritete/Rewi whānau — and her and Iri's interests were the subject of an exchange order (HK 17/315, 16.8.40). Page 5 repeats the Pati Wharewaka succession of 13.8.40 with her full name "Pati Wharewaka Topia" and Atama Matiu as trustee. Other Paihia 1D1C families: Ritete/Pirini/Tahana, Ihaka Uruhau, Hira Tukino, Herehana, Taitimu Tahana, Angel, Karaweia/Rameka/Matiu Kapa.

title: Waihapa — succession register 1880–1910: Hare Hongi Hika to Rongo Kahira, Mereana Paora, Tura Wiremu and five others (27 Feb 1890)
summary: Three pages of the Waihapa succession register (two handwritten register pages and a Form 16 schedule). Page 2: HARE HONGI HIKA, succession order 27 February 1890 (N4/119) to Rongo Kahira (m), Mereana Paora (f), TURA WIREMU (f), Rati Pona (m), Wini Tuta (m), Huia Miriama (f), Arihia Hemi (f) and Poni Rewharewha (f). This is the clearest Court record of Tura — "Tura Hongi" on the 1876 memorial, "Tura Wiremu" here after her marriage to Wiremu Tangata — succeeding to her father, and it fixes the membership of the Hāre Hongi Hika descent group that reappears as group A in the 1895 Pokaka title. Other entries: Ruinga Tapu (1880), Te Arama / Hone Kingi Tapu (1885), Hori Kerei, the Toetoe family (1890), Aporo te Meawai, Wakahe alias Te Hie, Meta Tapu, Erana Raupane alias Erana Ururoa (to the Snowden children, 1894), Mio Tuauru (1910).

title: Minute book 15 HK 261 — succession to Peri Paraihe alias Kaperiere Paraihe, whakapapa read in Court (25 Sep 1936)
court: Native Land Court, Tokerau District, sitting at Pawarenga
summary: Hokianga minute book 15, folio 261, 25 September 1936. Applications 246–258 (plus Paihia 1M3A and Wairoa A) — succession to Peri Paraihe alias Kaperiere Paraihe in fifteen blocks. The Court read out the whakapapa supplied by Mr Tamaho McMath: 1st wife Horomena Toriwhina = Peri Paraihe = 2nd wife Ruhia Matiu Wiripo. By the 1st wife: Maraea (deceased) = Rihari Matiu, whose children are Rirena Arama (f.a.), Tame Rihari Matiu (m.a.) and Whina Rihari Matiu (f., 18); and Ria Hone Wharewaka (f.a.). By the 2nd wife: Hone Peri Paraihe (m.a.); Okena P.P. (deceased), whose children are Rawiri Okena Peri (m., 15), Ngarimu (f., 9) and Hone (m., 13); Pirini P.P. (deceased, no issue); Arapeta P.P. (m.a.). Written approval of the whakapapa and request that all share in proper proportion lodged by Ria, Hone, Arapeta, Rirena and Tame; all present except Hone (ill). A will dated 5/8/27 lodged by Tamaho McMath at Rawene 9/9/36 was far too late for probate and the Court would not have approved its contents; the family agreed it be taken no notice of. Deceased died 7 September 1929. Orders: succession orders accordingly in favour of all nine as above; trustee for Whina to be [name illegible]; trustee for Okena's children to be Ria.

title: Otangaroa No 1 — memorial of ownership, 17 owners (Waipuna, Whangaroa, 9 Oct 1876)
court: Native Land Court, Northern District, Province of Auckland, sitting at Waipuna, Whangaroa
judge: Henry A. H. Monro; Wiremu M. Hikairo, Assessor
summary: Memorial of ownership under the Native Lands Acts 1873 and 1874 for Otangaroa (3,439 acres 2 roods), to be known as Otangaroa No 1: ordered on the application for subdivision that a memorial be inscribed in the names of Hare Hongi Hika, Paora Ururoa, Pororua Te Wharekauri, Haki Reweti, Ruinga Tapu, Patara Roro, Hema Ururoa, Hare Hongi, Hami Tuauru, Mita Hape, Karena Kiwa, Te Arama, Kerei, Kira, Marupo, Hare Napia and Keremeneta Peia. Fees: hearing £1, memorial £1. Marginal notes record later "5/- Propn" partition orders (1C1, 1C2… ) and "£1 transferred 18 O/S" (1919/1925 stamps). Hāre Hongi Hika — great-grandfather of Wiremu Arama through Tura — heads the list; the name "Ruinga" (one of his recorded names) also appears as the separate owner "Ruinga Tapu"; "Te Arama" is a further owner. Otangaroa 1C3B1, where Arama Taniora and Betty Hori held interests, descends from this title.
